KEY MESSAGE 1...As of 2:45 PM EDT...Sfc high pressure remains 
centered just northwest of the region. With large-scale subsidence 
and low-level dry advection, morning clouds have diminished with 
mainly clear skies across the region this afternoon. Afternoon highs 
will be mainly in the 50s to low 60s. With clear skies and 
relatively calm winds, temperatures will drop quickly after 
sunset, especially for northern/northeastern areas. However, 
increasing mid and high clouds overnight will cause temps to 
level out and eventually rise the second half of the night. Lows
will mainly occur before midnight, and will be in the upper 30s
to 40s. 

Tonight, a strengthening sfc low will track into the Great 
Lakes, and eventually towards the St Lawrence Valley tomorrow. 
This will lift a warm front northwards late tonight into 
tomorrow morning. Fairly strong warm advection/isentropic lift 
and a band of mid-level FGEN at the leading edge of a 
strengthening LLJ will allow for widespread showers to break out
across the region the second half of tonight into tomorrow 
morning. With some elevated instability across our area, 
isolated to scattered embedded non-severe thunderstorms are also
expected with these showers. PWATs increase to 1.5-1.75", so
some moderate to briefly heavier periods of rain may be
possible, making for a wet Friday AM commute. 

The LLJ strengthens to 50-60 kt early tomorrow morning, and while we 
will not mix deep enough for gusts that strong to make it down to 
the surface, winds gusts increase as the LLJ moves overhead. 
Maximum gusts look to be on the order of 30-40 mph, with a few 
isolated gusts to 45 mph possible along the west facing slopes 
of the Taconics/southern Greens and around the Capital District 
due to flow channeling. These winds could knock down a few large
limbs or trees, but are not expected to be strong enough or 
widespread enough to warrant advisory issuance. By mid-morning,
showers will be lingering for northern areas, but a break in 
shower activity is expected for areas from around the Capital 
District south and east. Temperatures will be several degrees 
above normal here, with some low 70s possible thanks to 850 mb 
temps of +14 to +16C. It will remain breezy in the warm sector, 
although the core of the LLJ moves off to our north and east 
before any breaks of sun/deeper mixing occur. 

Then, tomorrow afternoon and evening, the system's cold front tracks 
through the region as the sfc low tracks off to our north and east. 
Strong CVA and the right entrance of a jet streak to our north will 
provide forcing for ascent, leading to a line of showers and 
perhaps a few low-topped thunderstorms tomorrow afternoon ahead
of the cold front. SPC has expanded the marginal risk for 
severe slightly further north and introduced a slight risk for 
portions of southern Ulster/Dutchess/Litchfield counties, 
although confidence remains low whether we will see much (if
any) severe weather in our CWA. Limiting factors include: 
SBCAPE looks quite limited, with only 100 to possibly 250 J/kg,
and will be confined mainly to the southeastern Catskills and
Mid Hudson Valley. Additionally, there is a weak low-level cap
seen in forecast soundings that will lead to the presence of
some SBCIN. While a few breaks of sun are possible, much of the
area in question will likely see fairly extensive cloud cover
tomorrow as well that will limit the amount of destabilization.
Low-level convergence at the front does not look quite as
impressive in our area as for areas further to the south, as we
will see a more gradual wind shift to the W/SW and eventually
W/NW. Finally, any convection does not look to arrive in our
area until ~4 PM, at which point we will already be starting to
lose daytime heating. Low and mid-level wind fields remain
impressive, so this is not to say we won't have gusty winds with
this line of showers/storms tomorrow. However, confidence in 
these stronger winds aloft being able to mix down to the sfc and
reach severe levels remains quite low. 

The front moves off to our east early Friday night, with a much 
cooler airmass infiltrating the region in its wake. Showers come to 
and end for most of the region early Friday night, but lingering 
upslope/lake enhanced showers changing to snow showers are expected 
in the ADKs, southern Greens, and northern Catskills. By the time 
rain comes to an end, most areas will see a half inch to an inch of 
rain, with some locally higher amounts possible north of I-90. Given 
quick storm motions and long duration of the rain, no hydro issues 
expected. A coating to half inch of snow will be possible for the 
ADKs. Winds also remain gusty of out the W/NW Friday night through 
Saturday with deeper mixing in the cold advection regime and a tight 
pressure gradient across the region. Due to the very progressive
